x<-c (1+0i,2+4i)

## Variation & Co-variation using both Numerical & graphs
# Relationship between categorical and continuous variables
```{r}
data("iris")
head(iris)
```
```{r}
mean(iris$Sepal.Length)
```
```{r}
# Mean of Petal.length by setosa category
mean(iris$Petal.Length[iris$Species=="setosa"])
```
```{r}
# Mean of Petal.length by Versicolor category
mean(iris$Petal.Length[iris$Species=="versicolor"])
```
```{r}
# Mean of Petal.length by virginica category
mean(iris$Petal.Length[iris$Species=="virginica"])
```
```{r}
# Examine the mean by Shortcut
by(iris$Petal.Length,iris$Species,mean)
```
```{r}
# Examine the SD by Shortcut
by(iris$Petal.Length,iris$Species,sd)
```
```{r}
# Examine summary by Shortcut
by(iris$Petal.Length,iris$Species,summary)
```
## Visualize the differences in continouus variables btn categoarical using Box_and_Whisker plot

```{r}
boxplot(iris$Sepal.Length~iris$Species,data = iris,main="Comparison of Categorical VS Quantitative")
```
## Relationship btn two categorical variables
```{r}
ucba<-data.frame(UCBAdmissions)
head(ucba)
```
```{r}
# Cross tabulation # Contigency table
(cross<-xtabs(Freq~Gender+Admit,data = ucba))
```
```{r}
# Is there gender bias in UCB graduate admission process?
prop.table(cross,1)
```
## Simpson's paradox
# Phenomenon, where a trend that appears in combined groups of data disappears or reverses when broken down into groups.
```{r}
cross2<-xtabs(Freq~Gender+Admit,data = ucba[ucba$Dept=="F",])
prop.table(cross2,1)
```

## Data Management
# Create another Variable
```{r}
# Convert pounds to kilogram and Inches to meters
BMI<-(women$weight*0.453592)/(women$height*0.0254)^2
round(BMI,1)
```

```{r}
# attach it to data frame and get new data frame
women$BMI <-round(703*women$weight/women$height^2,1)
head(women)
summary(women$BMI)
```
```{r}
# Summary of BMI
summary(women$BMI)
```
```{r}
stem(BMI,scale = 2)
```

## Subsetting
# Creation of leadership data Interest: How men and women differ in the way they lead their organizations. 5 questions were asked in this study. Example of the question: Do men and women in management position differ in the degree to which they defer to superiors? 1: strongly disagree, 2: disagree, 3:neither agree nor disagree,4: agree, 5: strongly agree
```{r}
# Use of $,[] or [[]]
manager <- c(1,2,3,4,5)
country<- c("US","US","UK","UK","UK")
gender<-c("M","F","F","M","F")
age<-c(32,45,25,39,99)
q1<-c(5,3,3,3,2)
q2<-c(4,5,5,3,2)
q3<-c(5,2,5,4,1)
q4<-c(5,5,5,NA,2)
q5<-c(5,5,2,NA,1)
leadership<-data.frame(manager,country, gender, age, q1,q2,q3,q4,q5, stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
leadership<-data.frame(manager,country, gender, age, q1,q2,q3,q4,q5)
str(leadership)
```
```{r}
names(leadership)
```
# Missing Value
```{r}
leadership$age[leadership$age==99]<-NA
View(leadership)
```

```{r}
leadership$agecat[leadership$age>75]<-"Elder"
leadership$agecat[leadership$age>=5 & leadership$age<=75]<-"Middle aged"
leadership$agecat[leadership$age<35]<-"Young"
```
## One way of handling missing value
# Deleting all observations with missing data ( Listwise deletion) is one of the several methods of handling incomplete datasets. Note: You can also replacing the missing value by the average of the remaining data.

```{r}
is.na(leadership[,5:9])
```
```{r}
new_leadersh<-na.omit(leadership)
new_leadersh
```
# Sorting Data
```{r}
order(leadership$age)
```
```{r}
new_leadersh2<-leadership[order(leadership$age)]
```
## merging Data-sets
# To merge two data frame horizontally, you use merge() function. In most cases, two data frames are joined by one or more common key variables. -example 1: merge(dataframeA, dataframeB,by=“ID”) -example 2: merge(dataframeA,dataframeB, by=c(“ID”,“country”))

# the second merge the two dataframes by ID and country

# To join two data frame( datasets) vertically, use rbind() function: Note that the two data set must have the same variables

## Subset (selecting variables,dropping variables,selecting observation )
```{r}
new_ledersh3<-leadership[,c(5:9)]
(new_ledersh3<-leadership[myvars])
```
```{r}
new_leadersh4<-leadership[,c(-1,-2)]
(new_leadersh4<-leadership[,-(1:5)])
```
```{r}
new_leadersh5<-leadership[,c(-1,-7)]
leadership[[4]]
```
```{r}
new_leadersh6<-leadership[c(-1,-3),]
new_leadersh6<-leadership[c(2,4,5),]
new_leadersh7<-subset(leadership,age>=35|age<24,select=c(q1,q2,q3,q4,q5))
```
```{r}
attach(leadership)
```
```{r}
(new_leadersh7<-leadership[gender=="M" & age>30,])
```
